# Solar-system inspector sources (Stage 1)

All binary assets in this directory are bundled static files. The inspector requests the selected catalog body's reviewed local image only; it never contacts the source site at runtime and does not send observer, date, student, or account data. Credits below are shown in the in-app source panel as well as here.

## Reviewed but deliberately not bundled as first LOD

- Moon LOLA unsigned 16-bit elevation raster was reviewed (1440×720, 2,076,866 bytes; source https://svs.gsfc.nasa.gov/4720/). The verified conversion relative to the 1737.4 km reference radius is `(sample - 20,000) × 0.0005 km`, equivalently `sample × 0.0005 - 10 km`. The sample decoder is retained in `catalog.js`, but the raster is not applied as relief: the reviewed source page and TIFF metadata give no NODATA rule, so missing samples cannot safely be distinguished from elevations. No sentinel is guessed. This avoids telling learners that a speculative mask is real terrain.
- Mars MOLA elevation-color rendering is not included. The reviewed Mars image is a surface image texture only and is not an elevation layer.
- Saturn NASA VTAD GLB candidate (5,476,584 bytes / 5.22 MiB; https://science.nasa.gov/resource/saturn-3d-model/) exceeds the strict 5 MiB first-LOD budget and does not document embedded texture acquisition, date, filters, projection, or coverage. It is not loaded or presented as an observation. Stage 1 uses a small generated illustrative atmosphere texture and a few ring-band geometries with a schematic Cassini gap; both are clearly labelled as explanatory, and ring dimensions are not to scale. Cassini ISS PDS global FITS (about 74 MB; https://pds.nasa.gov/ds-view/pds/viewBundle.jsp?identifier=urn%3Anasa%3Apds%3Aco_iss_global-maps&version=1.0) is not bundled. Its small browse PNG contains chart axes/title and is not a globe texture.

## Illustrative bodies with no Stage 1 surface/atmosphere map

These bodies have no reviewed observation maps. Their smooth spheres and any generated atmospheric pattern are explanatory illustrations, not observed imagery:

- Venus: no reviewed Magellan radar map included; its in-memory cloud-like variation is illustrative only. NASA background: https://science.nasa.gov/venus/.
- Saturn: no Cassini observation map included; its ring bands and Cassini gap are stylized geometry only. NASA background: https://science.nasa.gov/saturn/.
- Uranus: no reviewed global map included; no named storm pins or detailed zoom. NASA background: https://science.nasa.gov/uranus/.
- Neptune: no reviewed global map included; no named storm pins or detailed zoom. NASA background: https://science.nasa.gov/neptune/.

For illustrative-only planets, a small in-memory generated grayscale modulation adds soft cloud-like tone variation to Venus, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune. These pixels are a visual treatment only; they are not observation maps, measured natural color, or current cloud patterns. Saturn’s ring is split into a few translucent stylized bands with a schematic dark Cassini gap; neither scale nor appearance is observationally registered. The selected shape/lighting is not a reconstruction of the selected observation time or physical rotation. No surface-location pins are supplied for any body in this first version. Observation-backed maps keep their source colors untinted.

## Asset handling

Bundled observation images are copied byte-for-byte from reviewed data-only assets and verified by the SHA-256 values above. There are no generated, sharpened, colorized, or height-painted observation maps in this bundle. Four explicitly illustrative bodies may create a tiny grayscale appearance texture in memory at runtime; it is not a downloaded or bundled map. The source catalog keeps types distinct: image mosaics, atmospheric map, and illustration. See the [NASA media use guidance](https://www.nasa.gov/nasa-brand-center/images-and-media/) for NASA content reuse, credit, third-party material, and endorsement restrictions. No NASA or ESA logos are used.

## Plan rulings

- Ruling: Mercury uses a small official MESSENGER mosaic preview as an educational image map, with source coverage and missing-data limits shown in the inspector. Venus's Magellan radar map remains deferred because no reviewed local asset is available; its model is explicitly illustrative and named above.
- Ruling: Saturn's GLB is not loaded because its measured 5.22 MiB size exceeds the automatic first-LOD budget and its texture provenance is undocumented. The low-cost globe uses explicitly illustrative in-memory shading plus stylized ring bands and a schematic Cassini gap, without implying a verified Cassini texture; cost if wrong: Saturn lacks an observation-backed cloud map in Stage 1.
- Ruling: Moon LOLA height is decoded only through a tested conversion helper but is not applied as displacement while NODATA remains unknown. Cost if wrong: the moon is a smooth globe with a real color mosaic rather than a relief model.
